engine.operational: Engine v2.3; Queensland: Engine v2.1.3 (v3 rating)
engine.release_note: v2.3 (27 Nov 2026 run on; approved by Damo 26 Nov): NSW, Vic, ACT, SA, WA and Tas ratings read past runs with 0.25 kg of credit for each extra kg carried (was 1 kg), and past margins become time figures at a fixed 0.170 s per length (was from each race speed); every layer refitted, display calibration refitted. The kg scale for these states changes from 0.226 to 0.269 per kg, so kg ratings read about 16% smaller: a change of units, not of any horse ability. Compare kg ratings within one engine only. v2.1.3 (27 Nov 2026 run on; approved by Damo 26 Nov): Queensland adds age and sex (age, 3yo and under, 7yo and over, filly or mare); Queensland display calibration refitted; Queensland kg scale unchanged. Ability ratings (opposition-aware, kg-equivalent) and time figures (margins converted to time; estimates, not measured times) remain separate inputs. Previously: v2.2 (26 Nov 2026 run on; approved by Damo 25 Nov): NSW, Vic, ACT, SA, WA and Tas add 14 Batch 10 terms (horses below their own proven level, own consistency, hot start to a preparation, quick backups, light weights, runs on file, rating certainty, measured venue class) and a recalibrated chance curve. Queensland: Engine v2.1.1, the v2.1 model refitted with Queensland country history (915 more meetings) and ages. v2.1 (25 Nov 2026, 12:17pm): Queensland ratings use the v3 rating, which expects lightly raced horses to improve (research/batch9 A; approved by Damo). NSW/Vic/ACT unchanged. v2.0.2 (12:06pm): win chances use the bent-line calibration. v2.0.1 (11:11am): Queensland scorer fix.
engine.previous: Previous engines (Engine v2.2 six states, Engine v2.1.1 Queensland) are scored every day as shadows from 27 Nov 2026. The original Engine v1 is a frozen benchmark; each engine's v1-style first layer is refitted on its own rating and is not the original
engine.scale: Ratings are kg-equivalent: model score divided by the score that 1 kg of opposition-aware rating is worth on average (Qld 0.224, NSW/Vic 0.269 per kg). They are relative to the average runner in the race. Contributions use the same divisor and add up to the rating. From 27 Nov 2026 (Engine v2.3) the NSW/Vic/ACT/SA/WA/Tas scale is 0.269 per kg (Engine v2.2: 0.226), so the same performance reads about 16% smaller in kg: a change of units, not of ability. Compare kg ratings within one engine only.

rules: A selection is the top-rated runner in the latest prediction saved before the race starts. It is frozen at that point and never re-created after the race.

The quoted price is the last price captured from a named source at or before 5 minutes before the scheduled start, stored with its source and time. TAB fixed odds and Betfair exchange prices are kept separate and never mixed.
Paper return: 1 unit to win at the quoted price. Selections with no quoted price are listed but excluded from paper returns (and counted).

Scratchings: a scratched selection is void (stake returned). Late-scratching deductions on fixed-odds winners are applied as published by the bookmaker; on Betfair, the exchange reduction factor is applied.
Betfair returns are shown after commission on net winnings, at the rate recorded with the quote.
Realised returns are only bets you actually placed and record yourself. They are never mixed with paper returns. Nothing here places bets.

checkpoints.status: Approved by Damo 27 Nov 2026 (Batch 17 brief s1): review checkpoints at 300, 1,000 and 2,000 settled, eligible, paired races per comparison; not automatic release thresholds
checkpoints.rule: Review each paired comparison at 300, 1,000 and 2,000 settled, eligible, paired races. At each review report the gain per race with its 95% interval, top pick and winner-in-top-3 differences, and consistency by state and by fortnight. Different candidates may need different sample sizes. A checkpoint is a review, never an automatic promotion. Original forecast timestamps, cutoffs and fingerprints are kept; no forecast is recreated.
checkpoints.why: The per-race spread of the difference between two engines is about 0.15, so the 95% interval is roughly +/-0.017 at 300 races, +/-0.009 at 1,000 and +/-0.007 at 2,000. Gains of the size measured in research (0.005 to 0.017 per race) need 1,000 to 2,000 races to tell apart from noise; the expected live gain is usually smaller than the research figure.

notes: Fit = how much better than random the winner's chance was (log-likelihood against a field-size baseline), as in every research table. Gains are log-likelihood per race on identical races, with a 95% interval.

Prospective = saved pre-race predictions judged on races run after the engine went live; never refitted on those races. Shadows and previous engines are scored before racing too, but are never shown as tips.
Historical figures are research results on past races, not live performance.

tracking.note: Tracked runs are shown for inspection. Only Queensland tracking feeds a model (the Queensland engine's closing-sectional and race-shape inputs); SA and Victorian tracking are not model inputs. Horses are matched by name, as the ratings are.

profile.note: Performance figures are each run measured against its field, in kg on the rating scale. Repeatable upper = second-best of the last six runs; one best run alone is not treated as sustainable ability.
